themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 16 this week versus a 7.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 106% increase (z-score: 3.13)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in CD305 this week.
evidence: 16 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Follows pattern of other street-level infrastructure degradation spikes in same period
reporting_angles: Walk the neighborhood to photograph illegal postings and map clusters—are they concentrated in one area or dispersed?
Contact DOITT/Sanitation to ask if there's a known gang or commercial poster active in East New York this week
Interview residents on whether they've noticed an uptick and what kinds of posters (political, commercial, gang-related) are appearing

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.6-complaint weekly average—a 380% spike (z-score: 4.91)—aligning with city budget requests for homeless services expansion and suggesting an acute street-level crisis.
evidence: 3 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
380% spike with z-score of 4.91 (highly statistically significant)
Community Board has requested expanded street outreach and new homeless shelters/SROs for multiple consecutive budget cycles—underlying issue persists
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners on where panhandling is occurring and whether they feel safe
Contact DHS and outreach teams to understand if there's a specific triggering event (shelter closure, weather, benefit disruption) driving the spike
Profile one or two unhoused individuals in the neighborhood to humanize the crisis and ask about access to services

themes_detail.label: Street Damage & Tree Vandalism Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged 400% (5 last week vs. 1.0 weekly average; z-score: 5.66) and damaged street signs jumped 229% (7 last week vs. 2.1 average; z-score: 4.18)—signaling either intentional destruction or severe infrastructure neglect in CD305 last week.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 5 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% spike, z-score: 5.66)
Damaged street signs: 7 complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average (229% spike, z-score: 4.18)
Two concurrent infrastructure damage spikes suggest either coordinated vandalism or systemic maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Visit specific blocks where tree damage and sign damage complaints clustered to assess whether damage is intentional vandalism or decay from neglect
Interview Parks Department and NYCOT to ask if they've noticed an uptick and whether enforcement resources are stretched
Ask residents whether they've witnessed or reported vandalism directly—are 311 complaints tracking actual destruction or is there a larger unreported problem?

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Reports Quadruple
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints hit 4 two weeks ago from a 0.9-complaint weekly average—a 357% spike (z-score: 3.37)—raising questions about restaurant sanitation or a specific outbreak event in East New York/Cypress Hills.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 3.37)
Coincides with period of elevated illegal posting and panhandling—possible indicator of broader neighborhood destabilization
No follow-up data on whether spike resolved or persisted into this week
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH to request data on which restaurants or food venues generated complaints and whether inspections have been conducted
Check if there was a specific food poisoning cluster (same restaurant, same pathogen, same event) or distributed cases
Interview residents about whether they or family members got sick and from which establishments

themes_detail.label: Inspection Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 4 last week versus 0.8 weekly average—a 433% spike (z-score: 4.91)—suggesting either increased enforcement activity or resident resistance to inspections in this district last week.
evidence: SPIT complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Unclear whether spike reflects increased city enforcement efforts or resident complaints about aggressive/inappropriate inspections
No corroborating data on what triggered the inspection surge
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH or relevant agency to ask what inspection blitz occurred last week and which properties/sectors were targeted
Interview residents or property owners who filed complaints to understand the nature of concerns (aggressive tactics, targeting specific groups, improper procedures)
Cross-reference with DOB permit filings (527 total in 90 days, 346 alterations) to see if inspections correlate with construction activity
